L751: 
L752: Let $f\in\mathcal{C}_{n+1}$. Then $f$ is an idempotent if and only if $\mathrm{Im}(f)\subseteq\mathrm{Fix}(f)$.

L755: Assume that $f$ is an idempotent, that is, $ff=f\circ f=f$. Then for any $f(x)\in\mathrm{Im}(f)$, we have
L756: 
L757:  | $$f(f(x))=(f\circ f)(x)=f(x),$$  |
L758: 
L759: proving $\mathrm{Im}(f)\subseteq\mathrm{Fix}(f)$.

L761: Conversely, suppose $\mathrm{Im}(f)\subseteq\mathrm{Fix}(f)$. Pick any $x\in[n+1]$. Then $f(x)\in\mathrm{Im}(f)$, and hence $f(x)\in\mathrm{Fix}(f)$. Therefore,
L762: 
L763:  | $$(ff)(x)=(f\circ f)(x)=f(f(x))=f(x),$$  |
L764: 
L765: which proves $ff=f$, and hence $f$ is an idempotent. ∎

L430: ## 4 Homomorphisms from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$

L432: In this section, we study the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma},\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})$ of all monoid homomorphisms from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$.
L433: ###### Theorem 4.1.
L434: 
L435: Let $\varphi:\{y_{1},y_{2},\dots,y_{m}\}\to\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ be a map defined on the generators of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$. The map $\varphi$ extends to a monoid homomorphism from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ if and only if there exist sets $X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{m}$ with $X_{i}\subseteq V_{\Theta}$ such that, for all $i,j\in\{1,2,\dots,m\}$, the following conditions hold:
L436: 
L437:   1. (i)
L438: 
L439: $X_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{\Theta}$;
L440: 
L441:   2. (ii)
L442: 
L443: $\varphi(y_{i})=e_{X_{i}}$;
L444:   3. (iii)
L445: 
L446: $p_{\Theta}(X_{i},X_{j})$ and $p_{\Theta}(X_{j},X_{i})$ both hold if $y_{i}$ and $y_{j}$ are not connected in $\Gamma$;
L447: 
L448:   4. (iv)
L449: 
L450: $p_{\Theta}(X_{i},X_{j})$ holds if $y_{i}\overset{\Gamma}{\to}y_{j}$.
L451: ###### Proof.
L452: Assume that the map $\varphi$ extends to a monoid homomorphism from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$, which we also denote by $\varphi$. Since a monoid homomorphism maps idempotents to idempotents, $\varphi(y_{i})$ is an idempotent in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ for all $i\in\{1,2,\dots,m\}$. By Proposition cite38†2.7 , $\varphi(y_{i})$ is of the form $e_{X}$ for some $X\in\mathcal{A}_{\Theta}$.
L453: Hence there exist sets $X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{m}$ with $X_{i}\in\mathcal{A}_{\Theta}$ for $i\in\{1,2,\dots,m\}$, such that
L454:  | $$\varphi(y_{i})=e_{X_{i}},$$  |
L455: 
L456: for all $i\in\{1,2,\dots,m\}$, which proves (cite60†i ) and (cite61†ii ). Now let $i,j\in\{1,2,\dots,m\}$.

L516: ###### Proposition 4.3.
L517: 
L518: The map $\Phi:\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma},\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})\to\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}_{\Gamma,\Theta}$ is a bijection.
L519: ###### Proof.
L520: 
L521: Let $\varphi\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma},\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})$. By Theorem cite65†4.1 , there exists a $(\Gamma,\Theta)$-admissible sequence $(X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{m})$ such that
L522: 
L523:  | $$\varphi(y_{i})=e_{X_{i}},$$  |
L524: 
L525: for all $i\in\{1,2,\dots,m\}$. Hence,
L526: 
L527:  | $$\Phi(\varphi)=(c(\varphi(y_{1})),c(\varphi(y_{2})),\dots,c(\varphi(y_{m})))=(X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{m}),$$  |
L528: 
L529: which proves that $\Phi$ maps into $\widetilde{\mathcal{S}}_{\Gamma,\Theta}$.
L530: Since every homomorphism from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ is uniquely determined by the images of the generators, since every homomorphism from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ maps generators to idempotents, and since idempotents in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ are uniquely determined by their content, $\Phi$ is injective.
